paragraphs.text: Read the component list before interpreting a combination. Intratumoral means inside a tumour and intravenous means into a vein; an accompanying checkpoint antibody may have either route according to the protocol. Record the injected material and lesion, every systemic drug and its route, and any radiation or ablation. Electroporation uses electrical pulses to support entry into cells; the injected gene payload and electrical delivery are separate intervention components. Track lesions whose injection status changes over time. Product manufacture, dosing procedures, monitoring and subsequent surgery or care belong in the study plan; a registry listing establishes neither benefit, local availability nor eligibility. DCIS, invasive breast cancer and melanoma are different populations, and a preoperative pathological response is not a survival endpoint.

paragraphs.text: In an invented single-arm study, twelve people each have an injected and an uninjected lesion, and all receive a systemic drug. At the stated assessment, injected-lesion responses occur in eight, uninjected-lesion responses in two and a defined blood immune-assay response in five. Each denominator is twelve, but participants can overlap: adding the counts to claim fifteen responders is invalid. These lesion counts do not provide the target-lesion, non-target and new-lesion information needed for a formal patient response category. Even all three observations in one person would not isolate the injection's contribution. Compare the combination with the same systemic treatment without the injected intervention, retaining population, endpoints, assessment timing, harms and appropriate control or blinding procedures.

paragraphs.text: Ho's single-arm phase 2 study combined radiation with pembrolizumab in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. The week-13 unirradiated-lesion endpoint yielded three responses among seventeen enrolled people, 17.6%, with a 95% confidence interval of 4.7% to 44.2%. Eight died from progression before week 13; among the nine assessed then, the same three responses were 33.3%, rounded to one decimal place. These are different denominators for the same numerator, not two treatment effects. Without a randomised systemic-treatment-only group, neither proportion estimates what radiation added or supplies a general abscopal probability.

paragraphs.text: Start with the goal and history before choosing a clock. A smaller lesion is a response observation at assessment; local control concerns keeping that site from progressing during follow-up. Postoperative local-recurrence prevention, relief of pain from a bone metastasis and a growing lesion during otherwise controlled metastatic disease are different questions. A meaningful pain improvement need not wait for an untreated tumour to shrink. A positive blood molecular test does not identify a lesion's position, boundary or safe access. An earlier scan date alone does not demonstrate improved outcomes. These distinctions organise evidence review rather than select a dose, procedure or treatment date. Nonmetastatic disease means no established distant metastases; a stage and subtype still need their own comparison of local and systemic care. Recovery, healing, previous exposure, overlapping toxicities and protocol assessment times supply other clocks. They are reasons to examine the studied sequence rather than invent a universal interval or repeat a procedure whenever a blood marker rises.

paragraphs.text: A local-treatment proposal needs five connected answers: the local and hoped-for wider outcomes with their measurements; evidence matching the cancer, disease history, complete strategy and comparator; access, intended coverage, margins, motion and nearby structures; actual exposure and normal-tissue risk; and alternatives, burdens and remaining uncertainty. In a fictional pair of equally sized lesions, proximity to a sensitive airway and a different approach can change feasibility. Depth alone is also insufficient: some deep lesions can be accessed, while a superficial lesion can have a difficult margin. Small diameter and a positive tracer scan settle none of the wider immune or outcome claims. Comparators can include systemic treatment alone, another local strategy, observation where appropriate or a study; include visits, recovery and additional sampling among the burdens. For a tracer and therapeutic product, establish the relationship between them rather than treating target uptake as a measured therapeutic dose. This review identifies missing facts and does not authorise treatment.

paragraphs.text: Delivery can be compared without ranking treatments. A fictional probe card controls a selected liver site, a beam card specifies a lung volume and motion assessment, and a radioactive-drug card requires distribution, retention and organ dosimetry. They are different routes, not a ladder from one lesion to invisible disease. A systemically distributed radioactive product still does not guarantee exposure of every microscopic deposit. Radiation injury does not require a conventional T cell to recognise peptide-HLA; proposed antigen-specific immune effects still need presentation, access, recognition and function. In another invented study, people receiving the same systemic strategy are randomised to a local addition or no local addition. With the same defined progression endpoint, starting time and follow-up, treated sites are controlled but new lesions occur in both arms and the progression-free-survival interval spans effects in both directions. That supports local control while leaving the added progression effect uncertain; survival, quality of life, pain and harms remain separate outcomes.

paragraphs.text: PACIFIC's five-year report concerns durvalumab versus placebo after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiation in unresectable, nonprogressing stage III non-small-cell lung cancer. The report found sustained progression-free and overall-survival benefit for that tested consolidation strategy. It did not require stereotactic body radiation, identify an abscopal mechanism or establish that focused radiation should always precede checkpoint treatment across cancers. Randomised comparisons, development phase and publication format answer different questions; these study cards cannot rank technologies from separate headlines. A case can describe a clinical course, a nonrandomised comparison can be distorted by treatment selection, and a model can supply a rationale for testing. These designs do not establish the same causal claim.

paragraphs.text: Oligoprogression describes limited progression within otherwise controlled metastatic disease during treatment. It is not restricted to one or two lesions or to targeted pills: the number, imaging rules and prior treatment depend on the definition being used. Oligometastatic disease describes limited detected distant spread, while limited residual disease describes what remains after treatment; retain the earlier burden and whether the remaining lesions are growing.

paragraphs.text: CURB was an open-label randomised phase 2 study after at least first-line systemic treatment, defining oligoprogression as at most five progressive lesions on CT or PET-CT. The prespecified lung cohort had median progression-free survival of 10.0 months with SBRT plus standard care versus 2.2 with standard care, hazard ratio 0.41, 95% confidence interval 0.22 to 0.75. The breast cohort had 4.4 versus 4.2 months, hazard ratio 0.78, interval 0.43 to 1.43. Failure to show a breast-cohort improvement does not establish an exact zero effect or a precise effect in every breast subtype. The intervention, comparator and harms must stay with the population.

paragraphs.text: NRG-BR002 tested adding ablation to first-line systemic therapy in breast cancer with at most four metastases, controlled primary disease, at most 12 months of first-line therapy without progression, and all visible sites amenable to SBRT or resection. Of 129 enrolled patients, 125 were eligible for analysis and 79% had HR-positive/HER2-negative disease. In the protocol-specified phase 2 go/no-go analysis with a December 20, 2021 data cutoff, median progression-free survival was 23.0 months without ablation and 19.5 months with it; the hazard ratio was 0.92, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.57 to 1.47 and stratified P = .42. Overall survival did not differ significantly and the study did not proceed to phase 3. This does not supply a definitive effect for every subtype or erase a separate symptom-relief goal.

paragraphs.text: NRG-BR002's accessible NIH author manuscript distinguishes its protocol-specified phase 2 analysis from non-protocol-specified extended follow-up with a September 4, 2025 cutoff. The latter reported median progression-free survival of 23.0 months without ablation versus 29.5 with it, hazard ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.60 to 1.44, and overall-survival hazard ratio 0.94, interval 0.56 to 1.60. These are separate analyses, not interchangeable updates to one median. The indexed abstract reports overall-survival hazard ratio 1.07 and stratified P = .52. Fifty-six of sixty assigned to ablation received SBRT, about 93%; this was not BOOSTER's probe-based comparison. Table 1 has ten triple-negative participants among 125, 8%, and 99 with hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative cancer. The report does not precisely establish every subtype's effect, and confidence intervals crossing one do not prove zero effect. The authors' recommendation against routine use outside trials retains a separate palliation exception.

paragraphs.text: BOOSTER randomised 65 selected patients with residual advanced lung cancer after checkpoint treatment, rather than the planned 137; its primary analysis included 42 with ablation and twenty without. The primary progression-free-survival clock began at immunotherapy initiation, before randomisation, so its medians of 26.7 versus 11.7 months include a selected pre-entry period. The report separately gives a randomisation-clock analysis of 17.1 versus 4.4 months. These clocks cannot be exchanged when comparing headlines. The physician selected freezing or heating: the abstract says thirteen cryoablation and 31 thermal-ablation patients, whereas Figure 3 and the discussion say thirteen and 29 among the 42 analysed. The discussion also notes larger lesions in the thermal group and no correction for multiple comparisons. This internally discrepant, exploratory comparison does not establish universal superiority of freezing or an immune-optimal modality.

paragraphs.text: STING normally sits in the endoplasmic reticulum; in the cells tested it moved to perinuclear compartments on activation, and palmitoylation at the Golgi was essential for activation (Mukai et al., 2016). That is intracellular trafficking, not release of STING as a circulating messenger.

paragraphs.text: The consequence depends on the cell. Host STING was needed for spontaneous CD8 T-cell priming against tumours in mice (Woo et al., 2014). In chromosomally unstable tumour models, ruptured micronuclei spilled DNA into the cytosol and activated cGAS and STING, and continuing chromosome segregation errors promoted invasion and metastasis in a STING-dependent manner (Bakhoum et al., 2018). A later study reported interferon tachyphylaxis and an endoplasmic reticulum stress response downstream of chronic STING activation in such cells, and an association of chromosomal instability and cGAS activation in micronuclei with immune suppression and metastasis in human triple-negative breast cancer (Li et al., 2023). An interferon RNA signal in a tumour sample cannot identify the producing cell or the sensor behind it, and acute and repeated stimulation can differ, which is not a rule that short stimulation helps and long stimulation harms.

paragraphs.text: Vanpouille-Box's 2017 experiments found that sufficiently high single radiation doses induced the DNA-degrading enzyme TREX1, reducing cytosolic DNA and interferon signalling. The threshold sufficient to clear cytosolic DNA varied from twelve to eighteen gray across the tested mouse and human carcinoma cell lines; a patient-derived lung-cancer xenograft was also examined. The work connected repeated lower-dose irradiation, type I interferon and dendritic-cell-dependent T-cell effects in defined models with checkpoint blockade. It does not supply a universal human dose ceiling, show that more physical injury always gives more useful immunity or select an individual radiation schedule.

paragraphs.text: A tumour specimen can contain malignant, immune, stromal and normal cells. A difference in an aggregate molecular signal can reflect a changed mixture, changed expression within cells or both. That is different from a directly counted cell fraction or a density per sampled area, each of which also needs its denominator and sampled region.

paragraphs.text: Preparation can change what is recovered. Slyper and colleagues compared single-cell and single-nucleus profiling in matched tumour specimens and found similar cell types at sometimes different proportions. A recovered profile mixture is therefore not automatically the original tissue census. Deconvolution and purity models can help investigate contributions under assumptions; they do not certify the cell of origin of every signal or remove sampling differences.

The immune count remains ten. Loss of other cells can raise the fraction without additional immune-cell entry; these observations alone do not establish recruitment, recognition or killing. This simple cell fraction is not the clinical stromal tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte score, which has a different denominator.

paragraphs.text: A second invented comparison starts with ten cells in one square millimetre of viable edge from lesion L. Follow-up A counts ten in the same stated area and region of L, giving ten cells per square millimetre at both times under the supplied assumptions. Follow-up B counts ten in 0.2 square millimetres from an injured centre of lesion M, giving fifty per square millimetre. B does not show a rise within L. Retain the lesion, viable area, centre or edge, collection time, treatment context and counting method. An early sample can capture transient injury signals and a later one a changed surviving-cell mixture. Equal area does not make separate tissue pieces identical, and matched sampling alone still cannot establish recruitment causation.

paragraphs.text: Measurement layers ask different questions. Anatomical imaging describes structure; tracer imaging depends on the stated product and its distribution; immunohistochemistry localises a protein in sampled tissue; bulk RNA pools captured messages; receptor sequencing describes recovered sequences and their sampled abundances; and controlled recognition or killing assays test a specified function under their conditions. RNA abundance is not accessible surface protein. Formenti's lung-cancer radiation-plus-ipilimumab study used clinical, blood-repertoire and selected functional readouts together; none is a universal immune-success marker or a substitute for the other measurements.

paragraphs.text: Biologically effective dose, or BED, is calculated from a radiation pattern and a specified tissue-and-endpoint model. In the basic equal-fraction linear-quadratic calculation, both total dose and dose per fraction matter, together with the assumed alpha/beta ratio. The result is a modelled quantity reported in gray, not extra physical dose.

paragraphs.text: For equal brief external-beam fractions, the basic linear-quadratic expression is BED = n × d × [1 + d/(alpha/beta)]. Here n is the count, d is dose per fraction in gray and alpha/beta is a tissue-and-endpoint parameter in gray, so the ratio inside the bracket is dimensionless. The simplified expression assumes negligible repair during delivery and complete repair between fractions, and omits overall time and repopulation. Prolonged or internally distributed irradiation needs additional modelling; this expression does not automatically compare every brachytherapy or radioligand pattern.

paragraphs.text: Two invented patterns, fifteen fractions of two gray and five of six gray, each total thirty gray. At an assumed alpha/beta of three gray, their BED values are fifty and ninety gray; at an assumed ten gray, they are 36 and 48. The between-pattern difference is forty under the first assumption and twelve under the second. These assumed parameters are not measurements of a person's cancer or organs. Lower alpha/beta gives fraction size more weight at fixed total dose; a low-ratio tumour narrows a contrast inferred using a ten-gray tumour assumption.

paragraphs.text: The linear-quadratic model expresses the surviving cell fraction after dose d as exp(-alpha × d - beta × d squared). The alpha/beta ratio is a parameter in gray for a specified tissue and endpoint. At fixed total physical dose, a lower ratio gives fraction size greater weight. Historical teaching values near ten gray for many tumours and early-responding tissues such as skin and mucosa, and three for late normal-tissue effects, are conventions rather than constants for every tumour or organ. A planned START-A/pilot meta-analysis estimated 4.6 gray for breast tumour control, with 95% confidence interval 1.1 to 8.1, and 3.4 for late photographic breast change, interval 2.3 to 4.5. The trialists interpreted these estimates as similar fraction-size sensitivity for breast cancer and its dose-limiting normal tissues.

paragraphs.text: FAST-Forward randomised 4,096 people after surgery for early breast cancer to forty gray in fifteen fractions over three weeks, 27 in five over one week, or 26 in five over one week to the whole breast or chest wall. Its five-year report found 26 in five non-inferior for ipsilateral breast-tumour relapse under the prespecified margin; the five-year relapse estimate after forty gray was 2.1%. Normal-tissue assessments differed by regimen: 27 produced more effects, whereas 26 did not show that increase versus forty. These are local-control and normal-tissue results in the tested setting, not a demonstration that a five-visit course is SBRT or an immune optimum.

paragraphs.text: Keep physical portions and their custody separate from reusable data. The record links collection site and time, treatment context, preparation, represented region and cells, prior use, remainder, holder and permitted use. Permission to analyse a dataset does not itself permit transferring or consuming its source block. For an authorised physical use, track the portion, sender, recipient, handling, receipt, consumption and remainder at each handoff. A returned block does not restore cut or extracted material. Diagnostic evaluation, patient safety and applicable consent take priority; the receiving laboratory and pathology must resolve actual suitability rather than infer it from quantity alone. Before allocation, specify the question, receiving method, minimum usable input, processing and transport timing, assay controls and what remains for other needs. These are method-specific requirements rather than a universal number of biopsy cores.

paragraphs.text: In an invented archive, one FFPE block came from a breast lesion collected on teaching day zero after systemic treatment. The last pathology review identified a mixed region of tumour, scar and immune cells. Diagnostic sections were cut earlier, but usable depth and relevant remainder are unknown. Pathology holds the block and must establish its diagnostic reserve; permission covers named molecular and image projects but no physical transfer. Lab A accepts FFPE and requests four five-micrometre sections: hold cutting until pathology confirms suitable remainder and the laboratory confirms input and permissions. Lab B requires living tumour cells: reject this fixed block for that request and ask which compatible input would be needed, without authorising another collection. The image team may reuse the already permitted teaching image version one from the last reviewed slide level without new cutting, recording its version and source slide. This is a complete allocation decision despite a named hold, not a standard section count or reserve percentage.

paragraphs.text: Match the named request to the actual preparation. FFPE can support a validated fixed-tissue assay if the relevant region remains, but cannot supply the original living cells. Snap-frozen material needs a compatible method and handling history; molecular preservation does not establish viable recovery. Viably cryopreserved material needs a suitable recovery protocol and the relevant living cells checked. Fresh tissue needs the receiving laboratory's processing and transport requirements. Blood or leukapheresis may suit a specified immune-cell or comparison workflow but does not substitute for tumour; a plasma cfDNA or ctDNA assay has its own collection, handling and timepoint requirements.

paragraphs.text: RNA, short for ribonucleic acid, uses ribose and usually uracil in place of DNA’s thymine. It is often single-stranded but can fold through internal pairing. Messenger RNA carries a coding template; ribosomal RNA contributes to ribosome structure and catalysis; transfer RNA brings amino acids; regulatory RNAs influence other molecules. Many nuclear messages receive a 5-prime cap and poly(A) tail and have introns removed by splicing before translation, but these features are not universal to all RNAs. Ribosomes read a coding sequence in codons to produce a polypeptide; processing, folding and localization follow.
